analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date and adds a 'Focused Gemma 4 tensor-parallel checks' section (head lines 1232-1345). I examined both head units, including the new section and the surrounding test guidance, against the threat model. The section describes test procedures only: model-free plan checks, CPU/GPU unit tests with synthetic weights, and oracle scripts over loopback or a local ring. It adds no executable code, workflow, endpoint, key handling, or configuration change, so it adds no attack surface and weakens no control for TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, A-003, A-008 or T-041. Statements about the Gemma prompt-prefix SSD tier (lines 1272-1291) say the records are encrypted and owner-only, that stale, corrupted and other-key records are refused, and that the daily write cap and free-space floor hold. These are consistent with the T-041 posture and do not claim any change to TTL, HMAC naming, or scope. The doc says that gemma caches long-context prefixes with SSD tier and a repeated request restores from SSD. That matches the existing T-041 per-donation gating description. No residual integration questions follow from this documentation-only change. I did not verify the referenced scripts or tests exist, since they are outside the supplied evidence. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of a problem.
